manual_title: Sterimax SA-600 Steam Sterilizer: Operation and Maintenance Manual (synthetic)

sections.title: 1.4 Pressure, steam and lockout
sections.text: The chamber and jacket hold steam under pressure. 1. Never try to open the door unless the chamber pressure gauge reads 0 bar and the chamber temperature is below 80 °C. 2. Before any repair, end or abort the cycle, close the steam supply valve SV-1 and lock it; switch the electrical isolator Q0 to OFF and lock it; attach danger tags. 3. Open the chamber vent valve and wait until the chamber and jacket gauges both read 0 bar. 4. Pipes, door and chamber surfaces stay hot: wear heat-resistant gloves and a face shield.

sections.title: 2.1 Machine overview
sections.text: The SA-600 is a jacketed steam sterilizer with a hinged door. The door seals with an inflatable silicone gasket that sits in a groove around the door frame and is pressed against the door by compressed air during the cycle. A liquid ring vacuum pump removes air during the pre-vacuum pulses. Condensate leaves the chamber through the drain, where a PT100 sensor measures drain temperature, then through strainer ST-2 and the steam trap.

sections.title: 4.2 E-07 Door seal fault
sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-07, door seal pressure not reached within 60 seconds of cycle start; the cycle does not start or is aborted. Likely causes: a cut, flattened or hardened door gasket; dirt in the gasket groove; low compressed air supply (below 5 bar); a faulty seal supply valve. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer and make sure the chamber is at 0 bar and below 80 °C (section 1.4). 2. Inspect the whole gasket for cuts, flat spots and hardening, especially near the hinge. 3. Clean the groove with a lint-free cloth and water for injection. 4. Replace a damaged gasket with door gasket SA-DG-600: press it evenly into the groove starting at the top centre, and apply a thin film of approved silicone grease SA-SG-01. 5. Check compressed air supply is at least 5 bar. 6. Run a vacuum leak test (limit 1.3 mbar/min) and a Bowie-Dick test; both must pass before the sterilizer is released. Typical time: 90 minutes.

sections.title: 4.3 E-12 Vacuum level not reached
sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-12, the chamber does not reach the pre-vacuum set point; the cycle aborts. Likely causes: no seal water to the liquid ring vacuum pump, an air leak at the door gasket or a valve, a worn vacuum pump. Procedure: 1. Check the seal water flow to the vacuum pump (sight glass must show flow). 2. Run a vacuum leak test: above 1.3 mbar/min means a leak; check the door gasket first (section 4.2). 3. If there is no leak, ask maintenance to service the pump with kit SA-VP-KIT. Typical time: 60 minutes.

sections.title: 4.4 E-21 Drain temperature low
sections.text: Symptom: alarm E-21, drain temperature below 121 °C during the exposure phase; the cycle aborts and the load is not sterile. Likely causes: strainer ST-2 blocked with scale, a stuck steam trap, wet steam. Procedure: 1. Lock out the sterilizer (section 1.4). 2. Open the strainer cap and clean screen ST-2; replace a damaged screen with SA-STR-2. 3. Blow down the steam trap; replace a trap that stays closed with SA-ST-15. 4. Check the PT100 drain sensor reading against a calibrated probe; replace a faulty sensor with SA-PT100. 5. Run one empty cycle and check drain temperature stays at or above 121 °C for the whole exposure. The aborted load must be treated as not sterile and reported to QA. Typical time: 60 minutes.

sections.title: 4.5 W-05 Jacket pressure slow rise
sections.text: Warning W-05 appears when the jacket takes more than 10 minutes to reach working pressure. The cycle continues but takes longer. First actions: check the plant steam supply pressure; check the jacket steam trap and strainer for blockage. Repeated W-05 warnings often come before E-21 drain temperature faults.

sections.title: 4.6 W-09 Feed water conductivity high
sections.text: Warning W-09 appears when the steam generator feed water conductivity is above 5 µS/cm. Scale and poor steam quality follow. First actions: inform the water system owner; check the purified water supply; increase blowdown frequency as per the maintenance plan.

sections.title: 6.1 Return to service after a repair
sections.text: 1. Remove locks and tags, open SV-1 slowly and let the jacket heat up. 2. Run a vacuum leak test: the leak rate must be 1.3 mbar/min or less. 3. Run a Bowie-Dick test cycle: the indicator sheet must show an even colour change. 4. QA reviews the test results and releases the sterilizer. 5. Record the repair, tests and downtime in the equipment logbook.

error_codes.title: Door seal fault
likely_causes: Cut, flattened or hardened door gasket
first_actions: Lock out: chamber at 0 bar and below 80 °C
Inspect the gasket near the hinge
Clean the groove with water for injection

error_codes.title: Vacuum level not reached
likely_causes: No seal water to the vacuum pump
Air leak at the door gasket
first_actions: Check seal water flow at the sight glass

error_codes.title: Drain temperature low
first_actions: Treat the aborted load as not sterile and tell QA
Lock out and clean strainer ST-2

error_codes.title: Chamber over-temperature
first_actions: Do not open the door until 0 bar and below 80 °C
Call maintenance to check the control valve and sensor

error_codes.title: Jacket pressure slow rise
likely_causes: Blocked jacket steam trap or strainer
first_actions: Check the jacket trap and strainer

error_codes.title: Feed water conductivity high
first_actions: Increase blowdown as per the maintenance plan
